correctness.rationale: The binary-quadratic discriminant is a smooth conic, so a projective line has either two reduced intersections or one double tangent intersection; PGL2 is transitive on each type, giving the two normal forms. Hwang–Li's rank-\(2\) construction then gives the displayed parametrizations. The secant equations are a codimension-two quadratic complete intersection of degree \(4\), singular along its boundary line; the tangent equations are the \(2\times2\) minors defining the smooth cubic scroll. Exact linear preservation of each quadratic ideal gives cone automorphism dimensions \(5\) and \(7\), with Euler-weight decompositions \(3+2\) and \(1+4+2\). Hwang–Li Theorem 1.4 then supplies the stated sharp bounds and equality characterization.

value.rationale: The initiating paper emphasizes that the correct symmetry algebra contains hidden grading-shifting symmetries and leaves the upper bound in terms of the symbol-dependent Euler-symmetric automorphism algebra. The two-dimensional quadratic pencil is the smallest case where that right-hand side is not forced by a single quadric. The exact dichotomy shows that a geometric degeneration of the pencil from secant to tangent changes the sharp bound from 5 to 7 and creates a negative-weight hidden symmetry, while simultaneously changing the equality model from a nonnormal quartic to a smooth cubic scroll. This gives a natural, complete low-dimensional test case for the new symmetry theorem and isolates a concrete mechanism for symmetry enhancement.
